label: monk2-s8
summary: The model approximates the MONK-2 rule (positive when exactly two of a1 to a6 sit at their first value; the 113 such training rows have outcome rate 100%, the other 232 have 0%) with two counters on opposite sides. A too-few gate (node 584) pushes the score down hard when a row has fewer than two first values: it is on in each such training row (0 of 89 have it off) and enters the score with weight -5.80. It is built from a tally of first values among a1, a4 and a5 and a detector (node 516) that fires when at least two of a2, a3 and a6 are first (and weakly in one other cell) and then switches the gate off. The too-many side is carried by direct edges, chiefly the first values of a5, a4 and a1 (-3.98, -3.70, -2.03 per sd), plus the detector's own edge (-0.92). The same direct penalties make it miss pairs that include a4 or a5: mean predicted risk 34% on those 45 positive rows against 80% on the other 68 positive rows. Over the 432 cells of the input space it agrees with the rule on 364; training accuracy is 85.5% and AUC 0.946.

tool_bugs: Not a code bug, a modelling limit: an annotation's entry nodes count as covered, so a downstream leaf cannot take another leaf's exit (516_b) as its entry; worked around by an identity node on 584 (the tally leaf) and putting node 584 in the composition. query_ablate(direct=true) reports no direct edges once the output has an identity node (the edges then belong to the direct_terms leaf); edge weights were taken from query_ablate(edges=[...]) instead. query_probe allows at most two sweeps, so the twelve detector cells took two probes.
